"boundary": "EasyCrypt models domain-separated H_context, H_post, H_accept, and H_state views of one abstract SHA3 operation, plus a separate keyed MAC_finished boundary for the implementation's HMAC-SHA3-256 Finished values. Its concrete bounded acceptance predicate requires the exact four-field current StateRevisionV1 recheck and the applicable peer Finished check, produces a key-plus-revision record, and has honest initiator/responder witnesses under both independent KEM directions. Equal non-bottom final secrets under distinct state identities imply H_accept or H_context input collisions; full-state and revision divergence add H_state, while post binding has a separate H_post collision lemma and Finished role/input binding is reduced only to an abstract MAC bad event. Checked semantic controls cover stale-current, wrong-peer-I/R, and explicit state/post/role/Finished-input omissions; the post ciphertext control is post-digest-only because ContextBound still absorbs that ciphertext. This is not a mechanized HMAC PRF/EUF-CMA reduction, Finished-forgery bound, temporal-ordering proof, crash/persistence proof, SHA3 proof, signature proof, concrete encoder correspondence, or formal-to-Rust/model-to-byte refinement. The Rust/Python frozen vector injects the same synthetic ABI2-boundary secret and checks TH through HMAC Finished values and K_acc, but does not independently derive K_abi2 from the complete ContextBound input; its bytes and source hashes are translation evidence only."

"boundary": "The symbolic model authenticates two independent role-owned capability offers under ideal pinned identity signatures before either role forms the ordered joint decision. It fixes role-separated HMAC-SHA3-256 values over one post-KEM transcript in protocol-role order: initiator Finished, responder verification/acceptance and responder Finished, then initiator verification/acceptance; Finished values are not signatures, neither offer signature depends on the peer signature, and there is no third commit flight. The Rust typestates and reference service follow that protocol-visible order independently of KEM encapsulation direction. The responder rechecks the exact local/witness head and verifies I before accepting, and exposes R only after durable reservation release plus bounded same-process accepted-key/response retention; the initiator similarly rechecks and verifies R before returning its retained key handle. IPC is a hard schema/domain V2 cut with no V1 fallback. Exact same-handle/same-Finished response recovery requires a newly signed nonce, the same live process, and the retained key; restart does not recover the key or cached R, while a durable capability-session tombstone prevents reuse. With uncompromised offer-signing keys and the modeled shared KEM key, matching accepted-key/session commitments agree on all modeled joint projections. The machine-checked status applies to the bounded symbolic theory. Rust tests and byte correspondence are evidence links only: the agreement and state/CAS theories are compositional, not an end-to-end formal-to-Rust refinement, and do not establish concrete signature, hash/KDF, KEM, transport, service, IPC, crash, or byte-code correspondence."
